evidence.note: Repeated verbatim sequential 'Plan:' lists (explore→read golden→read run_tests→build); a rough ordered checklist but with no per-step done-criteria or completion checks — matches the lower anchors.

Correctly identifies the layering (JSON-RPC/stdio transport, tree-sitter parse, then handlers) and sequences dependencies well: gets tree-sitter compiling and dumps AST structure before writing any handler. Workable dependency-first order — anchor 5+.

Writes all 12 LSP handlers in one monolithic push before any build or end-to-end test. No incremental 'initialize passing then first method end-to-end' milestone; only the full-suite run serves as a done-check. Falls short of anchor 8's incremental exit criteria.

In the debug phase it genuinely prioritizes by golden weight, citing case counts per method (selectionRange 10673, documentHighlight 10389 'close to working', implementation 322) — the anchor-8 behavior of weighting handlers by golden.jsonl frequency.

Mis-prioritizes by pouring 4+ steps into 60-case semanticTokens immediately after flagging hover/references/documentHighlight (10k+ cases) as the biggest opportunities — failing to defer low-value complexity, which keeps it below the top anchors.

reasoning: The agent clearly identifies the major layers and sequences dependencies correctly (transport/tree-sitter → AST verification → handlers), exceeding anchor 5, and during debugging it genuinely prioritizes method handlers by their golden.jsonl case weight (anchor-8 behavior). But it lacks explicit per-milestone done-criteria, wrote all handlers monolithically rather than proving one method end-to-end first, and mis-allocated effort to a 60-case method over its own identified high-count targets. This places it solidly between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 6.
